title: The Girl in the Margin
summary: Nao usually holds the viewfinder for her school art club. She wants to enter a drawing under her own name. When her secret portraits of the people beyond the frame go on the wall, one of her subjects asks for a different kind of picture.
coverAlt: The Girl in the Margin. In a brush-ink portrait, Nao looks through a tilted square cutout with one eye and reaches forward with her brush. A sketched face and a tiny folded chair stand beside her.
style: Original black-and-white school-life manga, brush ink with engraved screentones and open paper. Pages and dialogue read from right to left.

pages.alt: Ren offers Nao the square cardboard viewfinder in the art room. When she lifts it, only one of her eyes shows through the opening.
pages.transcript:
Nao? We need your steady hands again.

Everybody knows my hands.

pages.alt: Nao looks past her easel at Sora posing in the bright studio. Beyond it, Gaku holds the reflector, Hana handles a tray and Sora’s feet move beneath the stand.
pages.transcript:
Perfect. Hold it there.

Outside the square, nobody holds still.

pages.alt: Ren pins a square exhibition sheet and a narrow name strip to the board. Nao hugs her own square as she leaves the room with her classmates.
pages.transcript:
One square. One artist’s name.

Even mine?

You have to hand it in by noon Friday.

pages.alt: Sora poses with her ponytail held high. Seated on the platform, Sora tugs at her shoe and sock while Nao watches from behind her sketchpad.
pages.transcript:
Do I look peaceful?

My left sock is escaping.

pages.alt: Gaku holds a large reflector by its edge. Nao picks out his gripping hands in her sketchbook.
pages.transcript: A little higher? Is that better?

pages.alt: Hana sits in the stairwell with her mug and bun. Out in the doorway Nao quietly sketches her.
pages.transcript:
Ten minutes. Then I’m back on the tea table.

The cup fit exactly between her hands.

pages.alt: Sora folds a tiny chair during a break. The real paper chair sits in front of a row of carefully posed portraits.
pages.transcript:
I make one every time the timer sticks.

None of the drawings have chairs in them.

pages.alt: Nao measures the space around her model. Ren tilts a mount beside his glasses while Nao makes room on the table for a long strip of paper.
pages.transcript:
What if I draw the rest of the room?

A whole room in a square?

I know where to put the edges.

pages.alt: Under a lamp Nao makes separate little studies. She surveys her line of portraits with her pencil poised.
pages.transcript:
Gaku’s thumb. Hana’s tea. Sora’s chair.

And my name at the bottom.

pages.alt: Ren and Nao stand at opposite ends of three taped pictures: Hana sipping tea, Gaku holding the reflector and Sora making her chair. Nao frames them between her hands as classmates approach.
pages.transcript:
Try it on the wall before you trim it.

For a minute, I had a whole wall.

pages.alt: Hana pauses in the doorway with her tray. Nao grips her pencil while Hana stands beside the drawing of her quiet break.
pages.transcript:
Where did you get that?

The stairs. Yesterday.

I meant, who said you could put me there?

pages.alt: Hana faces Nao with her mug in both hands. Nao silently peels the entire strip from the wall.
pages.transcript: Those ten minutes were mine.

pages.alt: In the corridor, Nao offers the portrait to Hana face down. Hana slips the drawing into her apron pocket.
pages.transcript:
You can have the drawing. Or I can tear it up.

Give it to me. I like my hands.

pages.alt: Sora looks through the pictures at the edge of the worktable. Nao shows her how she drew Sora bent over the tiny folded chair.
pages.transcript:
Could I see the chair drawing instead of my face?

I didn’t draw the chair. I drew you making it.

pages.alt: Nao moves a cardboard square over the drawings, then sees one of her own eyes framed in a reflection. She lays the little pictures face down.
pages.transcript:
I thought I’d found the people nobody saw.

I’d just made another frame.

pages.alt: Nao carries the little blank-backed cards to school. At the library chessboard Gaku reaches for one.
pages.transcript:
Tomorrow I’ll bring the blank sides.

Can I put something on mine?

pages.alt: Gaku holds a carved knight above the chessboard. His thumb leaves a dark print beside a little drawing of the knight and its move.
pages.transcript:
I’d like the hand that moves the knight.

Here. This thumb. It always leaves a smudge.

pages.alt: At the tea counter Hana presses the bottom of her mug to a card. She lifts it, leaving a gray ring.
pages.transcript: You can use this much of my tea break.

pages.alt: Sora selects a crooked chair from the paper furniture on the sill. Nao touches its back and Sora balances it in her hand.
pages.transcript:
I want the one I made when everybody drew me standing up.

A portrait you could sit on.

Only if you’re very small.

pages.alt: Ren bends over the collected cards. Nao studies a gap beside her untouched competition square.
pages.transcript:
Where’s the person who held the frame?

I didn’t leave myself any room.

pages.alt: In the dark window Nao studies her reflection. Her finished square self-portrait rests at her worktable the following morning.
pages.transcript: Turns out I don’t stand still either.

pages.alt: Ren holds the submission-room door for Nao. Beside it she pauses, fingers on her painted self-portrait.
pages.transcript:
It’s a good portrait. There’s still time to enter it.

I know. I wanted to hear them say my name.

pages.alt: At the table Nao matches her square to the smaller pictures and tears it along a fold. As the clock reaches noon, Ren looks up and Nao works at the table, fitting the torn parts of her portrait together.
pages.transcript:
I still want my name on it.

Beside theirs.

pages.alt: Sora looks through the little door made from two halves of Nao’s portrait. A hand pivots the painted wing to reveal the folded chair behind it.
pages.transcript:
Your face has a door now.

It swings both ways. Try it.

pages.alt: Gaku bends to table height to see through the layered accordion. Hana leans in to share his view through its openings.
pages.transcript:
My knight can see straight through the chair legs.

That wasn’t in anybody’s sketch.

pages.alt: A festival visitor compares the ribbon nearby with the long tabletop exhibit. Nao shows where the individual square entries hang and stands beside the group’s work.
pages.transcript:
Which one got the ribbon?

The square exhibition is through there. This is ours.

pages.alt: Hana returns to her cup-ring card. Nao points out the paper hinge. With both hands, Hana turns the card with its gray cup ring toward the inside of the folded display.
pages.transcript:
I’d like my tea break back now.

It’s hinged, too.

pages.alt: At dusk Sora looks through the changed arrangement toward her paper chair. Nao sits with her book to draw the exhibit as it is now.
pages.transcript:
It looks different from yesterday.

Good. We’ll need a different drawing.

pages.alt: At the next sitting Ren holds up the viewfinder again. Gaku takes it while Nao settles at the easel.
pages.transcript:
Next sitting. Who wants the frame?

Someone else. I’m drawing this time.

pages.alt: Gaku holds the square above the folded work. Beyond a half-open studio door, Nao draws at her easel. A close view of the painted half of her face and her ink-stained drawing hand fills the foreground.
pages.transcript:
Where do you want the edge?

Leave the hinge loose.
